notes.title: Relics Discovered & Battle Refined
notes.content:
Hello again, my friends!

We’ve got a smorgasbord of new content and mechanical tweaks ready to show off today: first, [b]we'll take a closer look at our freshly forged passive relics, then an in‑depth run‑through of our re-vamped dodge, heavy attack, and shield systems and as a cherry on top we garnish with some UI changes[/b]. 

Let's get into the action.

[h1]Passive Relics: Objects of Power[/h1]

[b]Passive relics are mystical artifacts left behind by celestial knights. And they’re the backbone of what will make Colt a powerhouse throughout your different runs. [/b]What roguelike/lite would be complete without em right? 

So today we’re spotlighting two fun examples:

[previewyoutube=lAK3MoiED40;full][/previewyoutube]

With passive relics we'll be aiming to[b] do the regular stuff like boost damage yada yada...we'll also make things more interesting by trigger these bonuses at various timings.[/b] For example, our lovely [b]Mimic Maiden will give you +60% Shadow, Poison, and Arcane damage boosts whenever you open a chest. [/b][b]So hopefully you'll be more enticed to explore and find the chests in each level.[/b] Some like the [b]1st Edition Holographic Swordlizard makes it so Rare and Mythic quality swords deal +100% base damage, but ONLY if you have Rare or Mythic items in your inventory. This might make you re-think how'd you'd like to cultivate your arsenal and item choices.[/b]

And every relic will of course also feature it's very own wacky icon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41514828/6ace90e749cbadae3a6277280180d7099864cbe7.png[/img]

Also note that we've made some updates to the item reveal UI. It's now a sword shape that displays information but it also gleams [i]oooo...shiny[/i].

[h1]Stamina? Just some guy I used to hang out with...[/h1]

After watching alot of the older play sessions and recent testing, [b]we decided the stamina mechanic and bar was more frustration than fun.[/b] So we ripped it out in favor of cooldowns and shield charges. Here’s precisely what changed because of that:

[previewyoutube=lcNtL9GjEpc;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Dodge and Heavy Attack Cooldowns:[/h3]
[b]Both dodging and heavy attack are now on a cooldown.[/b] They have their own separate own radial timers, complete with vfx when they refill. You can opt into an above‑character display for health and dodge status that stays visible, let it hide automatically after use, or turn it off entirely.

[h3]3 Charge Shielding:[/h3]
[b]Shields now use three charges that regenerate over time.[/b] Lose all charges and your next block leaves you guardbroken (which kind of never really came into play much before).

[h3]Dodge Cancel Freedom:[/h3]
[b]Since dodge is now a resource that's on cooldown, we felt that it also needed to become more powerful.[/b] For maximum responsiveness, [b]you can now cancel any light or heavy attack into a dodge, even after the attack has started.[/b] This gives you instant reaction power without feeling punished for committing to an attack if you have a dodge to spend.

[b]These changes are to push the idea that every dodge is a deliberate choice, shielding feels more meaningful when you don't have dodge available, and heavy attacks can pack more punch + uniqueness without being spammable.[/b]

As always, we're thankful for your support as we continue to sharpen Swordcery into a fine blade!

With much stab,
Don and Mike

notes.title: Sword Class Pt. 2 - Take Your Seats Everyone!
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome back friends![/h1]

[b]Let's continue getting some of you who are new to Swordcery acquainted with the rest of the Sword Classes, as well as show you a bit of the 2nd biome: The Tombs of the Forgotten. [/b]

[h2]Greatsword: Barbarians Rejoice![/h2]
[previewyoutube=gQ8_-PR4OAI;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Not to be confused with Titan Sword Class, Greatswords are ALSO big but not as slow on startup.[/b] They however do have [b]slower recovery to compensate for their big damage.[/b] It [b]features a 3 part light attack combo that ends in a flippady slam 2-hit ender for max devastation.[/b] Not to be outdone by the light attack, [b]the heavy is the classic barbarian style whirlwind.[/b] You're able to move around as a tornado of violence! What's not to love?

[h2]Rapier: Timing Is Elegant![/h2]
[previewyoutube=tjPmoiVAbIY;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]The Rapier Class has exceptional reach for a mid-speed Sword Class.[/b] While wielding a rapier you get a [b]3 part light attack combo[/b] that could slay the Count of Monte Cristo and whoever else may have betrayed him. [b]The heavy attack features a unique timing machine specific to the class.[/b] You [b]hold and release at just the right moment for a BIG POKE[/b] that does sizeable damage. [b]If you fail however, you're gonna get a dinky poke[/b] that does alot less damage and has wack range.

[h2]Dual Swords: The Damage Demons[/h2]
[previewyoutube=OD8xpfAMHmc;full][/previewyoutube]
Two is always better than one! And the Dual Swords class is proof of that. This class [b]sports a 4 piece light attack combo that ends in a BIG X.[/b] The first 2 attacks also hit all around you for more coverage and the 3rd hits front and back! [b]As for the Heavy Attack? It sends out a full-blown disc of pain, growing in size and duration the longer you charge it.[/b] Dual Swords are all about [b]coverage and speed[/b]! It definitely lets you slash circles around your enemies.

[h2]Enter the Tombs[/h2]
[previewyoutube=PrZIyiEsTxs;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=NUxSJqvbw2c;full][/previewyoutube]
Everything here seeks to stop you dead in your tracks! Along with the usual shardling enemies, [b]acolytes will try to encircle you with deadly ring curses and throw projectiles at you.[/b] And the ghosts, known as [b]Phantos, will come at you with sword swipes! When they get low HP, they even try to possess other objects like lanterns or coffins to nom on you.[/b] More enemy variants incoming too!

[previewyoutube=AHiszVSCh4k;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Also in the tombs are plenty of fun things to smash.[/b] Link would have an absolute field day in here! Ancient jars, chemistry sets, old tables, candelabra...[b]destroy it all![/b]

[h2]And last but not least...[/h2]
Here's another video about how we turn our concepts into a sword/swordcery power! Hopefully we can shock and delight you with some of these behind the scenes details. This one is inspired by the title of a movie:

[previewyoutube=c6125HskfyA;full][/previewyoutube]

Thanks for reading and hope you enjoyed the update!
Hammer on metal,
-Don and Mike

notes.title: Enrolling You Into Sword Class
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome to class everybody! [/h1]

It's the... [i]*checks sundial*[/i]... semester of Spring or something!

[b]Some of you have been following Swordcery for a long time, but for those of you who are just now getting some details on the project via these Steam news updates, we'd like to tell you about some cool stuff on top of mentioning things we've been working on.[/b]

Lets cut into it!

[h1]Sword Classes[/h1]

What are Sword Classes? In Swordcery, you'll come across MANY swords. [b]Each of these blades will belong to a specific "Sword Class."[/b] Currently, we plan to have [b]7 Sword Classes total: Shortsword, Titan sword, Dual Swords, Rapier, Greatsword, Katana, and Dagger![/b]

[b]Most important to note is that each of these classes offers a different kind of playstyle! The various classes have a different light attack combo + a different heavy attack.[/b] We've recently been improving the feel of each sword class' attacks so now is a great time to talk about some of the differences that will make them fun to use!

[h2]Shortsword: Quick and Impactful[/h2]

[previewyoutube=WtMte2Av2Dk;full][/previewyoutube]
The Shortsword Class is the ol' good and reliable boy. [b]Fast but not too speedy, and packs a medium punch! It features a base 3-hit light attack combo[/b] that has not too much recovery time, so you'll be slashing and able to move around without big delay! [b]The last and 4th hit of the light attack combo is planned to be a mid-run upgrade you can acquire which allows Colt to perform the turning slash which deals 300% damage![/b] It's much slower startup though so use with caution! 

[previewyoutube=0_X5cah_hMg;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]And its heavy attack? How about a nice multi-level charge up and release AoE![/b] The big all surrounding spin attack acts as a perfect "GETOFFAME" for times when there's simply just too many damn enemies around. One could ponder on if this sword class was perhaps inspired by a hero of time... 

[h2]Katana: Stylish and Deadly[/h2]

[previewyoutube=8e4lAKChop0;full][/previewyoutube]
The Katana Class is style incarnate. [b]It has slightly longer graceful slashes that reach further than the shortsword, but has a little more startup overall.[/b] [b]Even though it may be a lil' slower, the multi-hit light attacks more than make up for its shortcomings! Notably, the last portion of the light attack combo even scoops up enemies and sends them flying[/b] (sometimes into pits eeehehehe). As for the heavy attack, what katana combat animation set would be complete without a SICK iaido dash slash. [b]The heavy attack can be charged up to increase travel distance. It not only slashes through enemies with style, but it can also be used to clear gaps/pits.[/b] But fair warning, if used haphazardly you could definitely end up in a pit or unintentionally surrounded by enemies! 

[h2]Titan Sword: The Bigger the Sword, The Harder It Falls[/h2]

[previewyoutube=Oh0_WScqdgM;full][/previewyoutube]
Do you play Dark Souls with a big dumb sword? [b]Do you like using a weapon that takes 3 business days to swing? Well have we got the Sword Class for you my friend! This here is a Titan Sword and it's the largest and slowest class in our whole game.[/b] But of course, it hits like a semi-truck! [b]The light attack combo is a slow 3-hit that finishes with a wide sweeping blow and the heavy attack is a charge jump slam that can dunk of enemies from downtown and get you right into the mix.[/b]

We're still working on revamping the other classes, so we'll show those off to you later! They're equally as spicy :D

[h1]But wait, there's more![/h1]

[b]So as we mentioned there will be tons of swords for you to collect and each will fall into a respective Sword Class, but they will ALSO have a swordcery power that is unique to each individual sword.[/b] So to successfully navigate the treacherous biomes of Swordcery, you'll be utilizing the Sword Class' attacks + each sword's unique swordcery power on top of that.

[b]Here's a short video talking about how we take a sword from concept to completion and give it its own cool power:[/b]

[previewyoutube=Fzl3TBKEjNo;full][/previewyoutube]

Thanks for reading and watching! 

Cuttin' up the dance floor in ways much too literal for an establishment's liking,
-Don and Mike
